correctness.rationale: The empty graph has one valid state. In every nonempty 2-degenerate graph delete a vertex v of degree at most two; its deletion removes at most one triangle and leaves a 2-degenerate graph. Each valid coloring of the remainder extends at v with either color unless the other two triangle vertices agree, in which case the opposite color is forced. Each fiber is connected, and opposite singleton fibers would require flipping both neighbors, so adjacent base colorings have a common extension color. One can move within a fiber to that color before lifting each edge of a base path, and finish with a fiber move. This proves connectivity for the entire state space, not just for a special starting coloring. Complementation negates the signed imbalance; a path to the complement changes the red count by one per move and must cross the middle count(s), giving the parity optimum. For K₃∨independent m, a split central triple forces all leaves to its minority color. The singleton central vertex cannot flip because of the triple, a majority vertex cannot flip because of the minority vertex and any leaf, and a leaf cannot flip because of the original majority pair. The six states are therefore isolated for every m≥1. Peeling leaves gives degeneracy at most three, while the induced K₄ gives at least three. For the book, unlike hubs yield the two independent leaf cubes; equal hubs give exactly two states with all leaves opposite. Each equal-hub state has exactly two legal flips, to the corresponding corners of the two cubes. For red-leaf counts a,b in opposite cubes the two routes have lengths a+b+2 and 2m−a−b+2, so at least one is no longer than m+2. Each connector is within m+1 of any cube state; the two connectors are Hamming distance m+2 and attain it by a cube path. This proves the diameter and the direct red-weight census gives the displayed polynomial, including coinciding degrees. The supplied verify.py was inspected, not executed; it tests a finite domain and does not replace these arguments.

value.rationale: The result separates a regime in which all legal states communicate from a regime in which there may be no legal moves at all and discrepancy can grow without bound. The fiber-intersection mechanism explains the threshold, and the book computation describes an entire natural family of state graphs and its two bottleneck connections. The already covered balance existence result is not the basis of this assessment.
